title: Ind-etale base change for the closed etale support right adjoint
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $g:T'\to T$ be an affine morphism (the inverse image of every affine open is affine) of Noetherian schemes, where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume $g$ is locally ind-etale: on affine opens its ring homomorphisms are filtered colimits of etale algebras of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Form the Cartesian square $Z'=Z\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with $i':Z'\hookrightarrow T'$ and $h:Z'\to Z$. Work in bounded-below derived categories of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For any closed immersion $a:W\hookrightarrow V$ with open complement $b$, let $a^!$ denote the right derived functor of $F\mapsto a^{-1}\ker(F\to b_*b^{-1}F)$ [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel]. Write $g^*,h^*$ for exact inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $i_*,i'_* $ for closed direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$h^*i^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}i'^!g^*K\qquad(K\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)).$$
It is the adjunction mate of the closed direct-image base-change isomorphism $g^*i_*\cong i'_*h^*$: after application of $i'_*$ and this identification, its composite with the closed counit is $g^*$ of the closed counit $i_*i^!K\to K$. These comparisons are $A$-linear and commute with cohomological shifts and with composition of affine ind-etale base changes. No constructibility hypothesis on $K$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images), Tag 0A45 (lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle), and Tag 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic): ind-etale base change for the closed-support right adjoint, obtained from the open-complement triangle and strict-local stalk formula. This is an agent-formulated general interface for the locality used in Travaux de Gabber, Expose XVII, Definition 1.1.1 and Definition 1.4.1.

proof.text: Put $U=T\setminus Z$, $U'=U\times_TT'$, and write $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, $j':U'\hookrightarrow T'$ and $q:U'\to U$. The open and closed base-change lemmas give the two complementary immersions on $T'$. The open-subscheme theorem for Noetherian schemes implies that the inverse image under $j$ of every affine open of $T$ is quasi-compact; the same applies to $j'$. An open immersion has diagonal the identity of its source (its two projections identify $U\times_TU$ with $U$), so it is quasi-separated. Thus $j,j'$ are qcqs, as required in the strict-local direct-image results below. No separatedness or finite-type assumption on $g$ is used.

source.place: Tags 01OW (lemma-locally-Noetherian), 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology); quasi-separatedness from the definition in schemes.tex, Tag 01KK (definition-separated)

proof.text: Let $i^!_0F=i^{-1}\ker(F\to j_*j^{-1}F)$. The supported-kernel adjunction states both $i_*i^!_0F\cong\ker(F\to j_*j^{-1}F)$ and $i_*\dashv i^!_0$ on abelian sheaves, with $i_*$ exact. These statements hold for constant $A$-module sheaves: kernels, direct images and the indicated inverse images carry their induced $A$-actions, and naturality of the abelian Hom bijection says that $f\circ a=a\circ f$ holds for a map if and only if it holds for its transpose, for each $a\in A$. Exactness of coefficient forgetting detects exactness of $i_*$ on modules. Module sheaves have enough injectives. Apply the bounded-below derived-adjunction theorem with $L=i_*$, $R=i^!_0$. It identifies the specified $i^!=Ri^!_0$ as the right adjoint of termwise $i_*$ on $D^+$, with counit represented on an injective complex by the supported-kernel inclusion. The argument applies also to $i'$.

source.place: Tag 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic), support adjunction; bounded-below derivation with its counit normalization

proof.text:
Choose a bounded-below complex $I$ of injective $A_T$-modules representing $K$. For every etale $V\to T$, apply the restriction-kernel lemma to the monomorphism $V\times_TU\to V$ in $T_{\mathrm{et}}$: it gives surjectivity $I^r(V)\to I^r(V\times_TU)$. Hence
$$0\to i_*i^!_0I\to I\to j_*j^*I\to0$$
is a degreewise short exact sequence of module complexes. The open immersion is etale and restriction along an etale map preserves injective module sheaves; thus $j^*I$ computes $Rj_*j^*K$. The bounded-below right-derived theorem computes $i^!K$ by $i^!_0I$. The short-exact-complex triangle therefore gives
$$S_K:=i_*i^!K\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_K}K\xrightarrow{\eta_K}Rj_*j^*K\to S_K[1].$$
The counit is the one fixed in Step 2, and the second arrow is the open adjunction unit. The same construction gives the triangle on $T'$. Naturality of the short-exact-complex triangle and of derived comparisons makes these triangles natural in $K$.

source.place: Tag 0A45 (lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle), injective-resolution proof; constant-module restriction-kernel version of the same exact sequence

proof.text: The canonical closed exchange $c:g^*i_*\to i'_*h^*$ is an isomorphism already on sheaves. Indeed at a geometric point $t'$ outside $Z'$ both sides have zero stalk by the supported-image description of closed pushforward; at a point $z'$ of $Z'$ the inverse-image stalk identification and the closed-pushforward stalk identification identify both sides with the stalk at $h(z')$. The representative-section formula for underived exchange sends the germ of a section to that same germ, so these are identifications of the canonical map. Stalk conservativity proves the assertion. The formulas are $A$-linear. Since closed direct image and inverse image are exact, the same $c$, applied termwise, is the closed direct-image comparison on $D^+$. Localizing the exact adjunction $i'^{-1}\dashv i'_*$ gives that same adjunction on $D^+$. Its counit is the termwise closed counit $i'^{-1}i'_*\cong1$. Thus the adjunction Hom bijection, followed by this counit isomorphism, proves $i'_*$ fully faithful on $D^+$; in particular it reflects isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 04CA (proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward), Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), and the canonical exchange on representative sections

proof.text:
Define $\beta_K:h^*i^!K\to i'^!g^*K$ by transposing
$$i'_*h^*i^!K\xrightarrow{c^{-1}}g^*i_*i^!K\xrightarrow{g^*\varepsilon_K}g^*K$$
under $i'_*\dashv i'^!$. The mate bijection makes this a natural transformation and gives exactly
$$\varepsilon'_{g^*K}\circ i'_*(\beta_K)\circ c_{i^!K}=g^*(\varepsilon_K).$$
Thus it is the comparison prescribed in the statement; it remains to prove invertibility.

Fix a geometric point $t':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T'$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, and put $t=g t'$. Write $C=T_{(t)}$, $B=T'_{(t')}$ with structural maps $s:C\to T$, $s':B\to T'$. Strict-local invariance for ind-etale morphisms says that the canonical map $v:B\to C$ is an isomorphism over $T$. Form $U_C=U\times_TC$ and $U_B=U'\times_{T'}B$; the map $U_B\to U_C$ is its base change, hence an isomorphism. Consequently the exchange $E_v$ for the open immersion $U_C\hookrightarrow C$ along $v$ is invertible: the two isomorphisms of schemes identify their small etale sites, and under these inverse equivalences the exchange is the identity by its transposed-counit definition.

For any $F\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}})$ of abelian sheaves, let $P:s^*Rj_*F\to Rj_{C,*}F_C$ be the strict-local exchange, and let $Q:s'^*Rj'_*q^*F\to Rj_{B,*}F_B$ be the corresponding exchange over $T'$. The strict-local global-homology theorem applies to $j,j'$ by Step 1: it says that global sections of $H^n(P)$ and $H^n(Q)$ are isomorphisms for every integer $n$, including negative ones. The global-sections-to-closed-stalk isomorphism on strictly henselian local schemes is natural in the sheaf, so it identifies these maps with their closed geometric stalk maps. Thus $P$ at the closed point of $C$ and $Q$ at the closed point of $B$ are isomorphisms on all cohomology groups. This uses the complex version of strict-local continuity, not only its sheaf-in-degree-zero version.

source.place: Tag 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images), derived assertions and their proof; strict-local global sections as the closed stalk

proof.text:
Let $E:g^*Rj_*F\to Rj'_*q^*F$ be the original open exchange. Apply the derived exchange cube to the original square and its strict-local square over $v:B\to C$. With the canonical inverse-image composition identifications it gives
$$E_v\circ v^*P=Q\circ s'^*E.$$
At the closed geometric point of $B$, $E_v$ is invertible by Step 6 and $v^*P,Q$ induce isomorphisms on every cohomology group by Step 7 (the isomorphism $v$ sends closed point to closed point). The inverse-image stalk formula, exactness of stalks, and the inverse-image composition identifications identify the remaining map with $H^n(E)_{t'}$. It too is invertible for all $n$. Since $t'$ was arbitrary, derived stalk conservativity proves $E$ is an isomorphism. Coefficient-forgetting exchange compatibility now gives the same assertion for every $F\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, with the specified $A$-linear exchange map.

source.place: Tag 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images); canonical exchange composition as in sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 0E47 (remark-compose-base-change-horizontal)

proof.text: Apply exact $g^*$ to the triangle of Step 3; it remains distinguished by the exact-functor triangulated theorem. Compare it with the triangle for $g^*K$ on $T'$, using the identity on the middle term and the open exchange $E_{j^*K}$ on the last term, after $q^*j^*K\cong j'^*g^*K$. The right square commutes: the transpose defining open exchange, precomposed with the open unit, is that unit, by the adjunction triangle identity. Rotate the two triangles and apply TR3 to this square. Rotating back supplies a first-component map $\lambda:g^*S_K\to S'_{g^*K}$ with $\varepsilon'\lambda=g^*\varepsilon$. Under $g^*S_K\cong i'_*h^*i^!K$, full faithfulness from Step 4 and the adjunction bijection of Step 5 force $\lambda=i'_*(\beta_K)\circ c_{i^!K}$. Hence the actual prescribed mate is the first component of a morphism of these distinguished triangles.

source.place: Tag 0A45 (lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle); TR2 and TR3 and the unit/counit definition of the exchange

proof.text:
For every $n$, take the five consecutive cohomology terms
$$H^{n-1}(K)\to H^{n-1}(Rj_*j^*K)\to H^n(S_K)\to H^n(K)\to H^n(Rj_*j^*K)$$
in the two compared triangles, with $g^*$ applied in the first row. The middle comparison is $H^n(i'_*(\beta_K)\circ c)$, and the other four comparisons are isomorphisms by Step 8 and the identity on $g^*K$. The five lemma proves that the middle comparison is invertible for each $n$. Thus $i'_*(\beta_K)$ is an isomorphism in the derived category. Applying the left inverse $i'^{-1}$ from Step 4 shows that $\beta_K$ itself is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0A45 (lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle), its long exact cohomology sequence and the five lemma

proof.text:
All maps defining $c$ and $\beta$ are module maps, and the Hom transpose in Step 2 is $A$-linear, so the isomorphisms are $A$-linear. On bounded-below injective complexes, the supported-kernel counit is termwise inclusion. Shifting complexes shifts this inclusion and the closed exchange without changing either map; after the canonical derived shift identifications the shifted $\beta_K$ and $\beta_{K[n]}$ have the same transpose, hence are equal for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. For successive affine ind-etale maps $g_1:T_1\to T$, $g_2:T_2\to T_1$, write $h_1,h_2$ for the maps on closed subschemes. The closed comparison for $g_1g_2$ equals the composite of the two comparisons: on a representative section both restrict it to its pullback, and successive restrictions equal one restriction along the composite. The transpose of
$$h_2^*h_1^*i^!K\xrightarrow{h_2^*\beta_{g_1,K}}h_2^*i_1^!g_1^*K\xrightarrow{\beta_{g_2,g_1^*K}}i_2^!g_2^*g_1^*K$$
is, by the two counit equations of Step 5, $g_2^*g_1^*\varepsilon_K$. This is also the transpose of $\beta_{g_1g_2,K}$, so the mate bijection gives their equality under the canonical composition identifications. The identity case is the same equation with the identity counit comparison. None of these arguments restricts the cohomology sheaves to be constructible.
